iPadOS 27.2 is releasing its beta version this week. In addition to introducing a redesigned Health app, Apple is also bringing over a feature that was recently exclusive to the Mac: a Siri window pops up when text is selected.

iPadOS 27.2 adds the feature of a Siri window popping up when text is selected, the same as in macOS Golden Gate

Siri AI is the headline new feature of iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and other simultaneous operating system updates. Apple has therefore provided multiple ways to launch this brand-new, upgraded assistant.

On iPad, you can wake Siri with the voice command "Hey Siri" or "Siri", swipe down from the top of the screen, open the new Siri option in the edit menu, open the new Siri app, or use my favourite method: press CMD + Space to open Spotlight, then ask Siri from there.

But iPadOS 27.2 adds yet another method, ported directly from the Mac.

In many situations in macOS 27 Golden Gate, when you select a passage of text, a small Siri icon appears in the top-left corner of the selection area. Move the cursor over it, and the icon expands to reveal the "Ask Siri" text input box.

iPadOS 27 itself did not have this feature. But now, if you have connected a trackpad to your iPad, iPadOS 27.2 offers the same experience.

As shown in the image above, the new Siri icon is initially very small and does not get in the way. Simply move the cursor over it, and the "Ask Siri" input box pops up conveniently.

If you don't have a trackpad connected, the full edit menu will still pop up when you select text, and you can tap to open Siri. However, with a trackpad, the entire experience is smoother and more seamless.

macOS is full of these kinds of small productivity-enhancing features that speed up daily tasks, but iPadOS has always lacked them. So it's truly exciting to see features that just appeared on the Mac being ported to iPad so quickly.

What are your thoughts on the new Siri pop-up window in iPadOS 27.2? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
